title: Finite positive cotangent Ext modules localize and vanish on the smooth locus
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $P$ be a commutative finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $N$ be a finite $P$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Use the full standard polynomial cotangent complex $L_{P/k}$ of [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data] and put $T^j(P,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P)}(L_{P/k},N[j])$ in the derived category of ordinary $P$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every integer $j\geq1$, $T^j(P,N)$ is a finite $P$-module. For every multiplicative subset $S\subset P$, the canonical localization map induces an isomorphism of $S^{-1}P$-modules
$$S^{-1}T^j(P,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^j(S^{-1}P,S^{-1}N).$$
Here module localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. If $\mathfrak q\subset P$ is a prime at which $\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then $T^j(P,N)_{\mathfrak q}=0$ for every $j\geq1$. Thus the support, defined by $\operatorname{Supp}_P T=\{\mathfrak q:T_{\mathfrak q}\neq0\}$, is contained in the nonsmooth locus. The assertion concerns positive cotangent Ext, not merely the first homology of the naive cotangent complex.

source.place: Tag 08PX, proposition-polynomial (finite polynomial resolution over a Noetherian base), Tag 08SF, lemma-localize, Tag 08R5, lemma-when-projective; flat localization of derived Hom is more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom. Compare examples-defos.tex lemma-first-order-localization for the degree-one argument.

proof.text: Every ideal of $k$ is either zero or all of $k$: an ideal containing $a\ne0$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$. Thus $k$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-polynomial-simplicial-resolution] to $k\to P$, obtaining $Q_\bullet$. By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], $E^{-n}=P\otimes_{Q_n}\Omega^1_{Q_n/k}$, with alternating faces and zero positive terms, represents the specified full $L_{P/k}$. For $Q_n=k[x_1,\ldots,x_{r_n}]$, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] applied to $k\to k$ gives the basis $\mathrm dx_i$: $\Omega_{k/k}=0$ since every $k$-derivation of $k$ vanishes. Consequently $E^{-n}\cong P^{r_n}$, so $E$ is a bounded-above complex of finite free modules. This uses no truncation of the cotangent complex.

Put $C^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_P(E,N[0])$, with the usual signed differential; its degree-$j$ term is just $\operatorname{Hom}_P(E^{-j},N)\cong N^{r_j}$ when $j\geq0$, and is zero when $j<0$. By [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], $E$ is K-projective. Acyclicity of its Hom into acyclic complexes says exactly that every chain map into such a complex is null-homotopic (degree-zero cycles are maps and boundaries are homotopies). Thus [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] applies and gives $T^j(P,N)\cong H^j(C)$. Explicitly a cycle is a map $E^{-j}\to N$ killing the preceding differential, hence a chain map $E\to N[j]$; boundaries are precisely null-homotopic maps. These identifications are $P$-linear and natural in $N$ and in maps of projective representatives.

source.place: Tag 064B (lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex); cycles and homotopies in the ordinary Hom complex.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $P$ is Noetherian. Each $C^j$ is finite, since a finite generating family of $N$ in each of the $r_j$ coordinates generates $N^{r_j}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], $Z^j(C)\subset C^j$ is finite. Its quotient $Z^j(C)/B^j(C)$ is finite, using the images of these generators. Step 2 therefore proves finiteness of $T^j(P,N)$ for every $j\geq1$.

Let $P'=S^{-1}P$ and $N'=S^{-1}N$. The isomorphism $E\simeq L_{P/k}$ of step 1 is a chain of quasi-isomorphisms in $D(P)$; by the clause of [lem-trf-cotangent-augmentation-localization] that degreewise tensor with $P'$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, it gives $E'=E\otimes_PP'\simeq L_{P/k}\otimes_PP'$, and composing with the quasi-isomorphism $\lambda$ of that node, $E'$ represents $L_{P'/k}$; it has finite free terms $P'^{r_n}$. In each degree the canonical map $S^{-1}\operatorname{Hom}_P(E^{-j},N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(E^{-j}\otimes_PP',N')$ sends $\phi/s$ to $(e\otimes a/t\mapsto a\phi(e)/(st))$. With the chosen finite basis of $E^{-j}$, both sides are $(N')^{r_j}$ and this map is the identity on the coordinates, hence an isomorphism. It commutes with the signed Hom differentials because these are precomposition with the matrix of $d_E$. Exact localization, including its cohomology comparison in [lem-trf-cotangent-augmentation-localization], gives $S^{-1}H^j(C)\cong H^j(\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}^\bullet(E',N'[0]))$. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] and [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] over $P'$ as in step 2. This proves the desired isomorphism, and the displayed formula identifies it with the canonical map obtained by localizing derived morphisms and extending $P'$-linearly. This works also when $0\in S$, when both sides are zero.

source.place: Tag 08SF (lemma-localize); explicit finite-free proof of the special case of more-algebra.tex Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), clause (3).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be a smooth point of $X=\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Choose $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $U=D(g)=\operatorname{Spec}P_g$ is an affine open on which this morphism is smooth. The affine-comparison clause of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] describes $L_{X/k}$ on the chart $X$ by the normalized complex of the standard resolution; by [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] (in the abelian category of $P$-modules, reindexed $n\mapsto-n$) that complex is homotopy equivalent to the alternating complex $L_{P/k}$, hence by step 1 to $E$. Sheafifying termwise preserves these quasi-isomorphisms (stalks, below), so the sheaf associated termwise to $E$ represents $L_{X/k}$. By the compatibility with restriction to the smaller affine chart $U$, $L_{X/k}|_U$ is $L_{U/k}$, and the smooth clause applied to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives $L_{X/k}|_U\simeq\Omega^1_{U/k}[0]$. The latter sheaf is finite locally free by [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free]: near $\mathfrak q$ it is $\mathcal O_U^r$ for a finite $r$. Take stalks. They preserve quasi-isomorphisms, since the kernel and cokernel statements in [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] identify the cohomology stalk with the cohomology of the stalk complex. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], the stalk of the termwise associated $E$ is $E_{\mathfrak q}$. Consequently $E_{\mathfrak q}\simeq P_{\mathfrak q}^{r}[0]$ in $D(P_{\mathfrak q})$. The comparison is an isomorphism of derived objects, not merely an assertion about one homology group.

Take $S=P\setminus\mathfrak q$ in step 4. Using step 5, its target is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P_{\mathfrak q})}(P_{\mathfrak q}^{r}[0],N_{\mathfrak q}[j])$. The source complex $P_{\mathfrak q}^{r}[0]$ is K-projective by [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], so [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] computes this as chain maps modulo homotopy. For $j\geq1$, the target has its sole nonzero term in degree $-j$, while the source is in degree zero. Every degree-preserving chain map is therefore zero. This proves $T^j(P,N)_{\mathfrak q}=0$. By the definition of support in the statement, none of these smooth primes belongs to the support, so the support is contained in the nonsmooth locus.

lean.statement: theorem cotangentExt_finite_localization_smooth_support (C : Coherence.{u}) (f : Arrow CommRingCat.{u}) (_hk : IsField f.left) (_hfinite : RingHom.FiniteType f.hom.hom) (N : ModuleCat.{u} f.right) [Module.Finite f.right N] (j : ℤ) (_hj : 1 ≤ j) : Module.Finite f.right (cotangentExt C f N j) ∧ (∀ S : Submonoid f.right, ∃ (ι : N ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (localizationSquare f S).right.hom).obj (localizedCoefficient S N)), (∀ n : N, ι n = LocalizedModule.mk n 1) ∧ ∃ e : localizedCotangentExtModule C f N S j ≅ cotangentExtModule C (localizedArrow f S) (localizedCoefficient S N) j, ∀ ξ : cotangentExt C f N j, IsCotangentExtLocalization C f N S j ι ξ (e.hom (LocalizedModule.mk ξ 1))) ∧ (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum f.right, (∃ U : (Spec f.right).Opens, q ∈ U ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth (U.ι ≫ Spec.map f.hom)) → Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl (cotangentExt C f N j))) ∧ {q : PrimeSpectrum f.right | ¬ Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl (cotangentExt C f N j))} ⊆ {q : PrimeSpectrum f.right | ¬ ∃ U : (Spec f.right).Opens, q ∈ U ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth (U.ι ≫ Spec.map f.hom)}
